title: NovaHealth — Hosted API: Semantic Ranking Pipeline Demo
next_steps: Schedule 1-week benchmark run with sample dataset

Marcus Lee — Email pricing and pilot terms to Raj and Elena (due 2025-12-04)

summary: Redwood AE + SE walked NovaHealth through a hosted API demo focused on semantic ranking: embeddings + reranker endpoints. Key topics: integration path, latency vs cost tradeoffs, Redwood Console optimize suggestions, data residency and SOC2, proposed pilot and runbook for a 1-week benchmark. Customer wants a hosted pilot but asked clarifying questions about VPC/private deployment and cold-starts for long documents.
topics: Redwood Console: route and model selection
transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone, um thanks for taking the time. this is Marcus from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
[00:12] Elena: hi, elena morales here, head of search at novahealth. we have raj and samir on the line.
[00:18] Raj: hey all.
[00:20] Samir: samir here.
[00:22] Marcus: awesome. today's goal is a hosted api demo focused on our semantic ranking pipeline — embeddings plus reranker — show you the console, the api calls, and an optimize recommendations quick tour. we'll leave time for questions. sound good?
[00:34] Elena: sounds good. quick context: we power clinical content search across docs and patient-facing FAQs. relevance is a bit spotty, and we want to move from BM25 + heuristic reranks to an embeddings-first approach. timeline is Q1 pilot, production later.
[00:50] Marcus: perfect. priya do you want to take the demo?
[00:54] Priya: yeah, thanks. i'll share my screen — tell me if you can't see — okay. first, the basic flow: you push documents into an embedding store, use /v1/embeddings to vectorize, then run a retrieval step, and finally call our /v1/rerank endpoint to score candidate passages. our hosted api can do both steps: embeddings for search and a lightweight reranker that accepts [candidate ids + embeddings] or text blobs.
[01:20] Samir: do you require a separate vector db?
[01:24] Priya: good question. you can use your own vector DB (we integrate with common stores) or use the lightweight in-hosted cache if you want a simpler path. for production at scale we often recommend pairing with an external vector DB like Pinecone or Elastic's vector features; but many customers start with Redwood-hosted embeddings + in-memory retrieval for the pilot.
[01:44] Raj: what's the typical latency for rerank? we're trying to keep QPS up with ~100ms p50 on single-pass queries.
[01:50] Priya: so for the hosted reranker endpoint under optimized configs we see p50s in the 70–150ms range for single-document rerank on our standard models for 128-token context. if you have long passages (500–1k tokens) that pushes latency up — we recommend chunking + prefix KV cache to avoid repeated work. note these numbers assume our n1 hosted pool; dedicated capacity gives tighter SLOs.
[02:14] Elena: cost is a concern — can you give me a rough delta between compact model + batching vs full-size model?
[02:20] Priya: roughly, compact model quantized profiles can be 3–5x cheaper per token, at some accuracy tradeoff. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and cache settings to target your latency SLO while minimizing token spend. we can show Optimize suggestions for your sample workload in the benchmark.
[02:38] Marcus: i'm going to walk through a simple api curl example i put in the deck: first call /v1/embeddings with the doc payload, you'll get back a vector. then run a nearest-neighbors query against your store and collect top-k, then call /v1/rerank with the query + top-k candidates. here's an example response — note the score field is normalized between 0 and 1.
[03:02] Samir: is the reranker always a separate model call or can it be combined in a generate flow?
[03:08] Priya: can be either — we support a combined candidate generation + score in one call for certain models, but separating gives you more control and cheaper reranks when you already have good candidates. combined flows are useful for generative answer surfaces.
[03:22] [03:24] Raj: are embeddings deterministic i.e., if i reindex will vectors be identical?
[03:28] Priya: mostly yes for the same model/version; if you change quantization or model variant you may get different vectors. we surface model versioning in the console and you can pin model ids for consistent reindexes.
[03:40] Elena: security question: we're in healthcare, need SOC2, encryption at rest with customer KMS, and audit logs. what do you support?
[03:48] Marcus: we have SOC 2 Type II, support customer-managed KMS for private deployments, and we emit audit logs. hosted customers get the standard set; for extra control we can discuss Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated lines. i'll share the security package after the call.
[04:05] Samir: what about data residency — if some PHI stays in eu region?
[04:09] Priya: hosted regions map to cloud regions — you can route requests to a eu region and pin the model deployment there. for strict residency we recommend Private (VPC) or on-prem.
[04:18] Marcus: ok, demo — i'm going to run a small live example, apologies if transcription picks up background noise.
[04:25] [04:27] Priya: here is a sample payload — i call /v1/embeddings, i get vector id 0x34f, i index into our test store, then i run a nearest-neighbor and get top 5 passages. next i call /v1/rerank with the query and the 5 candidates; response shows scores and final sorted order.
[04:47] Raj: seen the output — the reranker seems to demote long policy docs in favor of shorter faq snippets. is there a knob to prefer freshness?
[04:55] Priya: yes, reranker supports metadata priors — you can bias by publish date or by type. we also support signals like clickthrough or explicit relevance weights in the rerank payload.
[05:06] Elena: any pitfalls with long documents? our clinical notes average 3k tokens.
[05:12] Priya: for 3k tokens we recommend chunking into 256–512 token windows, generate embeddings per chunk, then store with parent-id for assembly at retrieval; for rerank we score chunks then assemble top chunks into a coherent answer. caching KV helps if queries repeatedly hit similar prefixes.
[05:30] Samir: what's the onboarding like — how quickly can we get a pilot?
[05:34] Marcus: typical pilot is 1–2 weeks to get a basic relevance baseline, 3–4 weeks for iterative improvements. for NovaHealth i think a 1-week benchmark run would be a good start — you provide sample docs and queries, we run both your BM25 baseline and our embeddings+rerank, and produce a quality + cost tradeoff report.
[05:53] Raj: ok. about billing — is pilot usage credited or do we get a small PO?
[05:57] Marcus: we usually offer pilot credits for hosted onboarding; if you want dedicated capacity we can do a committed term. i'll include pilot credit notes in the pricing email.
[06:07] Elena: developer experience: our team uses python. how ready are your SDKs?
[06:11] Priya: we have python and node sdks; the examples and quickstarts are in the console. larger customers can get a walkthrough of the api and an example runner for bulk reindexing.
[06:23] Marcus: also quick note on Redwood Console — you can see per-route latency, token cost, and per-model rollouts; i'll pull it up now.
[06:30] [06:32] Priya: screen shows the optimize tab — it ran an analysis on a simulated workload and suggests a quantized model + 32ms batching window to hit p50 120ms and reduce token spend 40%. these are heuristic suggestions you can accept or tweak.
[06:52] Samir: curious, how does optimize propose quantization without degrading quality?
[06:56] Priya: Optimize scores model variants against a small eval set you provide; it flags regressions by query and suggests fallback policies — e.g., run compact model by default and route specific queries to full model if the compact model falls below a quality threshold.
[07:12] Raj: any limitations on simultaneous rerank QPS?
[07:16] Priya: hosted pools are multi-tenant; we provide guidance and rate limits. for sustained high qps we recommend dedicated capacity where you get guaranteed throughput. we can show throughput curves in the next doc.
[07:28] Elena: let's talk about observability — if relevance degrades how will we know?
[07:32] Marcus: Console has eval dashboards and you can tie monitor hooks to your golden queries; we also emit traces for each request and can integrate with Datadog. Optimize can alert on metric drift.
[07:45] Samir: one technical nit — you mentioned prefix KV cache earlier — is that per-model or global?
[07:50] Priya: it's per-deployment, and you can configure TTL policies per route. it stores repeated attention / kv chunks for autoregressive generative flows; for rerank we use chunk caching where helpful.
[08:02] [08:04] Raj: another vendor comparison: with Elastic we're currently using hybrid search. what wins do you get with Redwood vs. Elastic?
[08:10] Marcus: two big things — operational simplicity (unified API + console) and inference optimizations (continuous batching, kernel selection, faster runtime for long-context rerank). Elastic's vector features are solid but you still have to manage model inference separately or fall back to simpler heuristics.
[08:28] Elena: internal question — our legal wants to see processor agreements and data flows. can you share redwood's DPA?
[08:34] Marcus: yes, that's part of the security pack i'll send.
[08:37] Samir: during the benchmark run can we test a private routing scenario? like model inference in eu + storage in us?
[08:44] Priya: cross-region introduces latency; you can route both inference and storage to same region. if you need mixed residency we can build a custom routing policy but for the pilot we recommend co-located resources.
[08:56] Marcus: quick demo wrap: here's a simple end-to-end script — i'll drop this in the follow-up email along with the console screenshots and the optimize export.
[09:05] Elena: great. any questions from your side?
[09:08] Raj: curious about retraining — if our labeling team provides feedback, how does that feed into rerank?
[09:14] Priya: you can push labeled examples into the eval tool, and Optimize will highlight systematic regressions; for models we can support fine-tuning flows or supervised ranking training off your labels — depends on how much labeled data you have.
[09:30] Samir: hmm, for cost forecasting do you provide a token-by-route estimate?
[09:34] Marcus: yes, console shows token projections by route and you can break down by embeddings vs rerank vs generation. we'll include an example cost model for your expected QPS in the pricing note.
[09:46] Elena: okay let's recap next steps.
[09:48] Marcus: recap: (1) NovaHealth to share sample dataset and golden queries — samir will send; (2) Redwood to run 1-week benchmark comparing BM25 baseline and embeddings+rerank; (3) Redwood to send pricing + SOC2 + DPA; (4) schedule benchmark kickoff next tuesday if that works.
[10:12] Samir: i'll send dataset by friday.
[10:15] Marcus: great. i'll put together calendar invite for the kickoff and include priya and the infra team.
[10:20] Elena: thank you both. quick aside — are there any gotchas you often see in clinical setups?
[10:25] Priya: watch for PHI leakage in prompts; enforce stricter redaction before indexing and use token-level scrubbing pipelines. also check anonymization knobs in the ingestion flow.
[10:38] Marcus: ok appreciate the time. we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed benchmark runbook. thanks everyone.
[10:45] Elena: thanks. bye.
